text:
alex: hey team — hitting a weird replay issue with the Python async client when using the same Client() across concurrent tasks. non-idempotent POSTs sometimes get re-sent after a 502 and we end up with duplicate creates.
jamie: can you paste a minimal repro?
alex: simple pattern:```py
async def worker(payload):
    async with Client() as c:
        await c.create_job(payload)
# spawn many workers concurrently
```
alex: when two workers overlap, i've seen the retry counter/state seem to leak between coroutines so the second call retries the first's request id.
alex: dug in — looks like we store mutable retry state on the transport/client instance (self._retry_state) and the async path reuses it without isolating per-request. race on _current_attempt counter.
maria: ahhh, right — we kept retry state at instance level for perf (to avoid allocating per-call) but forgot that async concurrency can mutate it.
jamie: quick fix options: make the retry context ephemeral per request (cheap to allocate) or clone/copy the instance-level state at request start.
alex: sketched a patch idea: in send_request() do something like `context = RetryContext(self._retry_config)` instead of mutating self._retry_state directly; avoid sharing mutable counters. also ensure we never mutate headers in-place (idempotency-key) across retries.
jamie: avoid deepcopy perf hit — better to keep client-level immutable config and create a tiny mutable context object per call (only counters + timestamps). that should be low-cost.
maria: agree. also add a guard so headers are copied before any in-place modifications: `headers = dict(orig_headers)` then mutate.
jamie: can someone add a flakey test that spawns ~50 concurrent tasks hitting a real-ish mock endpoint that returns occasional 502s to exercise the race? assert exactly N creates.
alex: i'll open a draft PR with the test + change and explain perf rationale. tagging sdk owners and linking to this thread. @jamie can you review the perf approach?
jamie: :thumbsup: will review. also add a changelog line and a short upgrade note about async client reuse semantics.
deploy-bot: automated: created issue #4821 from thread (py-sdk: async retry state race causing duplicate non-idempotent replays)
